stateTransitions: No product state changes.
alternatePaths: The source offer reflects the configured fork and the API document describes the running contract.
failurePaths: An invalid source URL refuses startup; unavailable metadata remains a conspicuous build-identity failure.

workflows.entryPoints: Login, logout, reauthentication, unauthenticated account recovery and own-account endpoints.
stateTransitions: Credentials create a server-side session.
Password or security changes revoke earlier authority.
Logout and session termination delete or invalidate sessions.
Locale and message choices update account preferences.
An unauthenticated recovery request by username issues a one-time credential and ends the account's sessions; one by address issues nothing.
alternatePaths: Initial credentials require a permanent password before ordinary use.
The current session can be ended without a second proof while other sessions require recent authentication.
A shared address holds several accounts, so the address path reminds each of its own name rather than issuing a credential per account.
failurePaths: Unknown, disabled and wrong-credential logins remain indistinguishable.
Expired proof, CSRF failure, rate limits and invalid password policy refuse without partial account mutation.
Recovery answers 202 for a subject that exists and one that does not, and swallows the per-account issuing limit so no refusal distinguishes them; the caller's own window answers 429.

workflows.entryPoints: Public configuration, courts, opening hours, cards, participant lookup and booking-grid endpoints.
stateTransitions: No product state changes.
alternatePaths: Uploaded branding replaces the configured URL fallback.
Anonymous and authenticated callers receive the same public availability without private fields.
failurePaths: Missing uploaded branding returns a typed not-found response.
Participant search and grid bounds reject invalid input without broadening the returned set.

workflows.entryPoints: Booking, participation, managed-appointment and recurring-series endpoints.
stateTransitions: A valid request creates a confirmed booking and court allocations.
Cancellation releases allocations and records its actor.
Participation withdrawal removes only the caller's participant record.
Series creation, move and cancellation change all selected occurrences transactionally.

Joining a waitlist stores one open entry per slot and account; a freed slot is offered to the first eligible entry in the transaction that freed it, and acceptance turns the reservation into a confirmed booking.
A holder publishes or withdraws a partner invitation for an own booking; an eligible member who accepts it joins the booking as a participant under the booking row lock.
A booking or cancellation the rules refuse is counted with its rule codes, card and the holder's membership type, in a transaction of its own.
alternatePaths: Booking-card roles and ADMIN authority select which appointments a caller may create or manage.
Series and move previews report blocked occurrences without mutation.
Before the instance reports ready, its warm-up previews a series and writes and cancels a booking inside a transaction it rolls back.
A disabled account or an entry no longer eligible is skipped, and an offer past its deadline is passed on by the waitlist sweep.
Open places list only invitations the caller may take, without names or booking ids, and the partner search sweep removes invitations nobody can take any more.
failurePaths: Rules, opening hours, unavailable resources and duplicate participants reject the whole write.
Unauthorized access is concealed as absence where existence would disclose another person's booking.
Concurrency and stale series state roll back rather than leave a partial calendar.
A reserved court refuses every other account's booking, and another account's waitlist entry answers as absent.
Another account's booking answers as absent to publish and withdraw, and an invitation the caller may not take answers as absent to acceptance.

workflows.entryPoints: The member's own check-in and the administrative attendance policy, attendance and no-show endpoints.
stateTransitions: An administrator switches attendance on or off and sets the release time.
The member who holds a booking checks in from 15 minutes before its start until its end.
An administrator records, replaces or clears the attendance of a started booking.
The release sweep cancels a started member booking nobody checked in for by the release time and frees its courts under the booking-grid lock.
A release tells the booker and every player of the booking once, in the centre and by mail unless they switched mail off.
An administrator lifts a person's counting no-shows, which stay recorded.
alternatePaths: Without attendance no check-in, release or no-show limit has any effect and recorded attendance counts for nothing.
A booking with nothing recorded is never a no-show, and a release records none.
failurePaths: Another account's booking answers as absent to check-in.
Check-in outside its window, on a cancelled booking or after a recorded no-show is refused.
Recording before the start, on a booking cancelled before its start or while attendance is off is refused.
A release time without attendance is refused.

workflows.entryPoints: Administrative court, opening-hour, season, holiday, court-closure, booking-card, participant-card and membership-type endpoints.
stateTransitions: Administrators create and correct configuration records.
Active flags retire and restore resources without deleting history.
Opening-hour changes schedule a weekly version from today or a later day; earlier days keep the hours they had, and a version not yet in force can be removed.
Storing a season, holiday or court closure tells the people in each booking it newly closes, once, and leaves the booking in place.
alternatePaths: Impact endpoints let the board inspect affected future bookings before a restrictive change.
Existing records remain readable and correctable after deactivation.
failurePaths: A change that would invalidate future bookings is refused with the affected state intact.
Invalid role, capacity, time or colour data returns field-specific violations.

workflows.entryPoints: Roster, membership, account, role, credential and session-administration endpoints.
stateTransitions: A person may gain or lose a current membership.
An account may be created, corrected, enabled, disabled or assigned a new credential.
Role and username changes revoke stale authority.
Session termination removes one account's or every account's sessions.
alternatePaths: A person may exist without an account and an account may retain non-member roles after membership ends.
Credentials can be issued for a new account or reset for an existing one.
failurePaths: The last enabled administrator cannot remove its own continuity.
Duplicate usernames, stale writes, invalid roles and missing recent proof refuse without partial security changes.

workflows.entryPoints: Import-source, external-reference, preview, execution and run-history endpoints.
stateTransitions: An import source defines the external identifier and field mapping.
An import source reads its files by header or, for an export without a header row, by stored column position and column count; switching between the two needs explicit confirmation.
An uploaded snapshot creates a preview bound to its reviewer.
Executing a current preview creates or corrects people, memberships and optional accounts, then records one run.
Missing source members lose the member role or receive the mapped membership state.
alternatePaths: External references can be linked manually before the next full sync.
A removal threshold requires explicit confirmation before execution.
failurePaths: A file read by position whose first row has a different column count is refused before a preview exists.
Malformed rows stay row failures in the preview.
Expired, superseded, stale or differently owned previews refuse transactionally.
Concurrent execution for one source serializes and cannot duplicate people.

workflows.entryPoints: Rule-set, rule-type, rule and club-configuration endpoints.
stateTransitions: Administrators create, correct, activate and retire rule sets.
Rules are added, replaced or removed by declared type.
Club identity, locale, time zone, booking grid, message validity and branding are corrected.
An uploaded logo becomes the effective same-origin image until removed.
alternatePaths: A default rule set applies when a member has no membership type.
Removing an uploaded logo restores the configured URL fallback.
failurePaths: Unknown rule types and malformed specs are rejected.
Changes that conflict with opening hours or future bookings fail without mutation.
Unsafe URLs and active-content uploads return field-specific failures.

workflows.entryPoints: Message template list, change, preview and reset endpoints.
stateTransitions: An administrator stores the club's own subject and body of one message in one language.
A reset removes that wording so the shipped wording applies again.
alternatePaths: A preview fills a wording with example values and stores nothing.
A stored wording the message cannot fill is skipped and the shipped wording is sent.
failurePaths: Unknown or missing required placeholders, a secret in the subject or a line break in it are refused with typed violations.
A change or reset without recent full-password proof is refused and changes nothing.

workflows.entryPoints: Impact, utilisation, usage, statistics, message-history, audit-log, bounded operational-log and operator-health endpoints.
stateTransitions: No product state changes.
alternatePaths: Impact reads page through all affected future bookings before a configuration write.
Reports use the club time zone; utilisation and usage reports stop at 366 days, statistics accept periods of at most 36,525 days in the years 0001 to 9999.
Message and audit records expose privacy-safe event metadata to the permitted board role.
Operational records come only from the fixed application, database and proxy sources and are redacted before bounded storage.
The usage report counts capacity by card and membership type, cancellations, attendance and refused attempts without naming a person, an account or a booking.
Operator health reads version, migration history, mail handover evidence, the public origin and the operator's backup record without changing any of them.
failurePaths: Unknown subjects, cross-scope cursors and invalid report periods refuse without disclosing another set.
Unavailable delivery evidence remains explicit rather than appearing successful.
A stopped collector, dropped input, rotation and an incomplete scan remain explicit rather than appearing as an empty complete log.
Operator health reports a check without evidence as unavailable and a failing check with the place that fails, never as healthy.

workflows.entryPoints: Roster, booking, audit-log, message-log and per-person export endpoints.
stateTransitions: A subject-access export records that the answer was produced; ordinary CSV exports do not change domain state.
An audit-log or message-log export records one whole-instance audit entry naming the log and the period.
alternatePaths: Roster and booking exports select bounded fields and periods.
Subject access assembles every record about one person while omitting other people's data.
Audit-log and message-log exports stream every entry up to the moment of the request in batches, optionally bounded by a period.
failurePaths: Unauthorized callers are refused.
Unknown people and invalid periods return typed failures without an empty or cross-person export.

workflows.entryPoints: Retention policy list, set and remove, retention preview and retention run endpoints.
stateTransitions: An administrator sets or removes how many months one record category is kept; no record changes.
A preview stores the cut-offs it judged against and the former members it would remove, for one account and a limited time.
A run pseudonymises bookings and series that ended before the cut-off and removes eligible former members with their accounts, then records counts only.

For the bookings and series it pseudonymised, a run clears actor and person or account fields from their change log entries and deletes their notification entries, queued messages and unfinished event publications.
alternatePaths: A former member who became ineligible after the preview is skipped and counted.
A former member eligible by date but still an administrator, named in a booking the run keeps or on a waiting list is reported as blocked and never removed.
Expired retention previews are deleted by the preview sweep.
Removing a period discards every open preview that applies it.
failurePaths: A preview without any configured category is refused.
A run without recent full-password proof, of another account's preview, of an expired preview or of a preview already run is refused and changes nothing.
A period outside one to 1200 months is refused.
